title: Viva Engage: broadcast, meeting-based and custom events with moderated questions and anonymous posting
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, December retirement deadline and both Teams control paths and commands are supported. The licensing discussion should distinguish published product licensing from unpublished feature-specific requirements, and several checklist controls are missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the new combination of broadcast, meeting-based and custom events with moderated and anonymous posting.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage events broadcast meeting custom moderated feed anonymous events landing page; "Engage events" "moderation" "anonymous". Read organize-live-event, send-calendar-invites and microsoft-viva-engage-features; results describe older live events, AMAs and invitations.

claims.claim: The Viva Engage service description gives April 15, 2026 as the retirement date for Engage live events powered by Teams Live Events.
claims.quote: Engage will retire live events powered by Teams Live Events effective April 15, 2026.

claims.claim: That service description says already scheduled live events remain supported through February 28, 2027.
claims.quote: Existing live events already scheduled will continue to be supported through February 28, 2027.

claims.claim: The service description encourages moving to Engage events powered by Teams town hall.
claims.quote: We encourage customers to transition to events in Engage powered by Teams town hall

claims.claim: MC1552394 was published on 13 November 2026.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; governance; rationales
claims.claim: Creation of new Teams town hall events from Viva Engage ends on December 7, 2026.
claims.quote: Starting December 7, 2026, users will no longer be able to create new Teams town hall events from Engage.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Previously scheduled Teams town hall events will run as planned.
claims.quote: Previously scheduled events will continue to run as planned.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice directs organisers to create town hall, community town hall or AMA events using Engage events in Viva Engage.
claims.quote: In Viva Engage: Create town hall, community town hall, or AMA events using Engage events.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The notice also permits creating town hall events directly in Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Teams: Create town hall events directly in Teams.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; front matter: action
claims.claim: The notice's act-by date is 2026-12-07.
claims.quote: Act by: 2026-12-07 (16 days from today)

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends informing organisers and communications teams before December 7, 2026.
claims.quote: Inform event organizers and communications teams about this change before December 7, 2026.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating documentation, training and guidance referencing the retired creation route.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, training materials, and guidance that reference creating Teams town hall events from Viva Engage.

claims.claim: In Teams events, organisers and co-organisers can enable moderation to review and approve questions before publication.
claims.quote: In Teams events, organizers and co-organizers can allow presenters to manage the Q&A sessions. They can also turn on moderation to review and approve questions before they appear in the Q&A feed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Anonymous questions in Teams Q&A are ingested into the organiser's mailbox for eDiscovery when anonymous posting is enabled.
claims.quote: If the meeting organizer enables anonymous posting, the questions attendees post are ingested into the organizer’s mailbox for eDiscovery.

claims.claim: Engage event invitations can reach subscribed internal and external community members subject to preferences and organisational policies.
claims.quote: Invitations can be delivered to subscribed internal and external community members, subject to their preferences and applicable organizational policies.

claims.claim: Send calendar invitations is off by default.
claims.quote: Send calendar invitations is off by default. You can create the event without sending attendee invitations and turn the setting on later by editing the event.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The event organiser manages the per-event Send calendar invitations option.
claims.quote: You must be an event organizer to manage event invitations. ... Create a new event or edit an existing event in Engage. ... Turn on Send calendar invitations.

claims.claim: Both Teams events attendee policy settings default to Everyone, allowing any user to attend events created under that policy.
claims.quote: By default, both settings are set to Everyone. When users with this policy create events with up to 1,000 attendees or events optimized for large audiences, any user can attend.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 groups above 5,000 members, an administrator must update delivery restrictions in Microsoft Entra to allow invitation delivery.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 groups with more than 5,000 members, an administrator must update the group's delivery restrictions in Microsoft Entra to allow invitation delivery.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to the new Engage event capabilities is published.
claims.quote: If you do enforce Viva Engage licensing, users access the Viva Engage Core experience, but each user must have the following: a Microsoft 365 license. a Viva Engage Core Service Plan.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/viva/engage/setup. Replace the blanket licensing absence in the notes, body and cost rationale with: 'Viva Engage Core comes with Microsoft 365; when Engage licensing is enforced, users need a Microsoft 365 license and a Viva Engage Core Service Plan. Feature-specific licensing for the new broadcast, meeting-based and custom event capabilities is not yet published.'

claims.claim: The service description links to Microsoft 365 plan comparisons and the Product Terms site rather than naming licences for the new event types.
claims.quote: For detailed plan information on subscriptions that enable users for Microsoft Viva Engage, see the Microsoft 365 business plan comparison and Microsoft 365 Enterprise plan comparison. ... For licensing terms and conditions ... see the Product Terms site.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Teams event capabilities and attendee capacity vary with the organiser's licence.
claims.quote: Event capabilities and attendee capacity vary based on the organizer's license.

claims.claim: No meter or separate charge is published for the new broadcast, meeting-based and custom event capabilities.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage broadcast meeting custom events pricing consumption charge meter; Viva Engage events license licensing Viva Engage Core Microsoft 365 events pricing meter. Read events-licensing, Engage setup and both Engage service descriptions; no meter for these new capabilities.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The default arrival state of the new broadcast, meeting-based and custom event capabilities is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage events default enabled admin switch Teams events policy AllowTownhalls QnAEngagementMode; "Engage events" "default" "admin". Read roadmap, supplied notices, Engage setup, organize-live-event and send-calendar-invites; no default for the new capability set.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes organisers moderating and attendees posting, not automated actions.
claims.quote: Organizers will have additional support for moderating the posted questions and conversations, and attendees can post questions anonymously.

claims.claim: MC1552394 identifies event organisers and communications teams as affected and names Viva Engage and Teams.
claims.quote: Event organizers who create Teams town hall events from Viva Engage. ... Communications teams responsible for organizing events. ... Microsoft Viva Engage ... Microsoft Teams

claims.claim: Teams Q&A requires sign-ins for the Office 365 Viva Engage service to be enabled in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: To allow users in your organization to add Q&A to Teams meetings and events, you must confirm that sign-ins for the Office 365 Viva Engage service are enabled in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience reaches the scheduling control.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. ... Select an existing policy or create a new one. ... turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled prevents organisers under that policy creating large-audience Teams events.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from creating events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Disabled

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting Engagement > Q&A reaches the Q&A control.
claims.quote: Open the Teams admin center. ... Expand Meetings ... select Meeting policies. ... Either select an existing policy or create a new one. ... Navigate to the Meeting Engagement section and toggle the Q&A setting On or Off.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -QnAEngagementMode Disabled prevents organisers with the Global policy from enabling Q&A.
claims.quote: To prevent organizers with this policy from using Q&A in meetings and events they create, use the following script: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity Global -QnAEngagementMode Disabled

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Turning the Teams event scheduling setting Off after scheduling prevents the organiser running or starting the event.
claims.quote: If you change the value to Off after a user schedules an event, they can't run or start the event.

claims.claim: Documentation does not establish the new Engage event feed's anonymous-question mailbox destination.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva Engage events anonymous questions eDiscovery organizer mailbox retention sign in prerequisites. Read manage-qna-for-teams, Engage setup and organize-live-event; results include general Engage retention but do not identify the new anonymous feed's mailbox.

claims.claim: The referenced Teams Q&A documentation provides organiser choices for moderation and anonymous posting, not separate admin settings for them.

Read manage-qna-for-teams and the settings-policies-reference search excerpt; found the Q&A admin toggle and organiser choices, not separate moderation or anonymous-posting admin toggles.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Teams events licensing overview does not state that it applies to the new events created in Viva Engage.
claims.quote: Searched: "Engage events" "license"; Viva Engage events license licensing Viva Engage Core Microsoft 365 events pricing meter. Read events-licensing and Engage setup; the overview describes Teams events and does not identify the new Engage event capabilities.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review attendee policy settings, calendar invitations and group delivery restrictions without corresponding control rows.
claims.quote: Check ... for who can attend; ... before turning on Send calendar invitations ... update delivery restrictions ... Table rows: Who can create Teams events ...; Whether organisers can use Q&A.
claims.fix: The Before rollout attendee-policy check and the At rollout calendar-invitation and delivery-restriction checks have no corresponding rows. Remove those checklist instructions; keep the supported descriptions in Risk assessment. Do not add unverified control rows.
